lines.text: one dead pig almost started a war.
June 1859. An American farmer, Lyman Cutlar, finds a big black pig eating his potatoes.
He fires. The pig drops. "That's my pig!" the owner roars.
"Ten dollars," says Cutlar. "One hundred," snaps the owner.
Both men live on San Juan Island, and both America and Britain claim it.
Britain threatens to arrest the farmer. "Send soldiers!" the settlers beg.
Captain George Pickett lands with about sixty soldiers and digs in.
Then British warships sail in, cannons pointed at the beach.
Picture two neighbors screaming over a fence while both families grab baseball bats.
The British admiral arrives, takes one look, and refuses to start a war over a pigsty.
Both camps sit on one island for twelve years, waiting on diplomats.
In 1872 Germany's emperor settles it. The island goes to America.
Final score: zero soldiers hurt. One pig dead.
Two empires nearly fought over a garden.
